title: Line-bundle triple data for a pinching square
statement: Let $X,A,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $v:A\to X$, $j:B\to X$, and put $W=A\times_XB$ with projections $a,b$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. All pullbacks below are tensor pullback of module sheaves [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define the canonical overlap $c_L:a^*v^*L\simeq b^*j^*L$ by composing the inverse of the adjunction-normalized composition comparison for $a,v$ with the comparison for $b,j$, using $va=jb$ [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. A line triple is $(M,N,\alpha)$ with $M$ invertible on $A$, $N$ invertible on $B$ [def-sc-invertible-module], and $\alpha:a^*M\simeq b^*N$. Compatible maps to $(M',N',\alpha')$ are arbitrary module maps $r:M\to M'$, $s:N\to N'$ with $\alpha'\circ a^*r=b^*s\circ\alpha$. A lift is an invertible $L$ on $X$ with isomorphisms $e:v^*L\simeq M$, $f:j^*L\simeq N$ satisfying $\alpha\circ a^*e=b^*f\circ c_L$. The predicate for specified $L,e,f$ is the same displayed equality. Define the line-equivalence predicate to mean that every triple has a lift and every compatible pair between the restrictions of two invertible modules is induced by exactly one module map between them. Define the affine-pinching-cover predicate by requiring each $x\in X$ to lie in an affine open $U$ whose inverse images in $A,B,W$ are affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that $\Gamma(A_U)\to\Gamma(W_U)$ is surjective and the canonical section-ring square $\Gamma(U)\to\Gamma(A_U),\Gamma(B_U)\to\Gamma(W_U)$ is cartesian in commutative rings, equivalently $\Gamma(U)\simeq\Gamma(A_U)\times_{\Gamma(W_U)}\Gamma(B_U)$. Define tensor triples componentwise, with overlap the tensor of the overlaps conjugated by the canonical pullback-tensor comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. The unit triple consists of the two structure modules, identified on $W$ by their canonical pullback-unit isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. For $p:X\to S$ and $t:T\to S$, define $v_T:A\times_ST\to X\times_ST$ and $j_T:B\times_ST\to X\times_ST$, and the map $W_T\to W$, by fibre-product functoriality. Define the pulled-back triple using the actual pullbacks of $M,N,\alpha$, conjugating the latter by the canonical composition comparisons. Pullback and tensor preserve invertibility [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. The comparison of the pullback of a line to a new branch with the pullback of its old branch restriction is the same canonical composition comparison. These are definitions of data and predicates, with no assertion that the line-equivalence predicate holds.
